paragraphs.notes: Caption line, flush left, above the first drawing. This is the caption the preceding page announced when it said the reaction of (II) with (III) is 'in Schema 1 angegebene'. The zh field holds the verbatim German, since this is a German-language WO publication and not Chinese.

paragraphs.zh: Die Dicarbonylverbindungen der Formel (II) sind entweder kommerziell erhältlich oder können gemäß bekannten Methoden hergestellt werden. Solche Methoden sind beispielsweise aus EP-A 0 283 261, Tetrahedron Lett. 32, 3063 (1991), J. Org. Chem. 42, 2718, (1977), Helv. Chim. Acta. 75, 2265 (1992), Tetrahedron Lett.  28, 551 (1987), Tetrahedron Lett. 32, 6011 (1991, Chem. Lett. 551, 1981, Heterocycles 26, 2611 (1987) bekannt.
paragraphs.en: The dicarbonyl compounds of formula (II) are either commercially available or can be prepared according to known methods. Such methods are known, for example, from EP-A 0 283 261, Tetrahedron Lett. 32, 3063 (1991), J. Org. Chem. 42, 2718, (1977), Helv. Chim. Acta. 75, 2265 (1992), Tetrahedron Lett.  28, 551 (1987), Tetrahedron Lett. 32, 6011 (1991, Chem. Lett. 551, 1981, Heterocycles 26, 2611 (1987).
paragraphs.notes: Transcribed exactly as printed, including four things that look like errors and have deliberately not been corrected: the stray comma in '2718, (1977)'; the full stop in 'Helv. Chim. Acta.'; the opening parenthesis in '6011 (1991,' that is never closed, so that everything from '(1991' to the final '(1987)' sits inside an unbalanced bracket; and the double space before '28,' at the line break. The journal titles are set in italics and the volume numbers in bold in the original; the run of citations is a bibliographic list with no German prose in it, so the citation text itself is identical in zh and en, and only the framing sentences differ. The German closes with the verb 'bekannt' governing the whole list ('Solche Methoden sind ... bekannt'), which English cannot keep at the end, so the translation moves 'are known' forward and drops the trailing word.

paragraphs.zh: Verbindungen oben genannter Formel (III) können gemäß bekannten Methoden aus Verbindungen der Formel (III), in der R für Hydroxy oder Alkoxy steht, hergestellt werden.
paragraphs.en: Compounds of the above-named formula (III) can be prepared according to known methods from compounds of formula (III), in which R stands for hydroxy or alkoxy.
paragraphs.notes: The same formula number (III) is printed on both sides of the sentence: compounds of (III) are made from compounds of (III). Read literally this is self-referential, and it is only coherent if the two occurrences differ in the meaning of R, which the sentence fixes for the second occurrence only. Transcribed and translated as printed rather than repaired; see discrepancies.

paragraphs.zh: Verbindungen der Formel (III), in der R1 für Alkoxy steht, können beispielsweise gemäß Schema 2 aus Verbindungen der Formel (IV), in der Hal für Halogen steht, hergestellt werden.
paragraphs.en: Compounds of formula (III), in which R1 stands for alkoxy, can be prepared for example according to Scheme 2 from compounds of formula (IV), in which Hal stands for halogen.
paragraphs.notes: The 1 on R is printed as a superscript and is rendered inline here because the transcription is plain text. 'Hal' is printed in ordinary roman type, not italic, and matches the Hal label drawn in Schema 2 below.
Caption line above the second drawing. It is indented very slightly further from the left margin than the 'Schema 1:' caption at the top of the page.

drawings.notes: Schema 1: condensation of the cyclic 1,3-dione (II) with the aroyl compound (III) to give the invention's compounds of general formula (I). Read as the invention's own route, not prior art, on two grounds visible on this page: the product is labelled formula (I), which is the invention's general formula, and the only prose on this page that touches the scheme treats (II) and (III) merely as starting materials that are commercially available or preparable by known literature methods. The sentence that formally introduces Schema 1 is on the preceding page and is not visible here. No SMILES is given for any of the three structures because every one of them is a Markush: Y and Z are variable ring members, v and w are variable counts, the (R7)w bond does not terminate on an identified ring atom, and R, R1 to R7 and L are all undefined on this page. The formula labels (II), (III) and (I) are printed in roman numerals in parentheses, centred below their structures; the (I) label sits noticeably higher than the other two because the product structure is drawn taller.

arrows.notes: A single long horizontal solid arrow with a filled head. Nothing is written above it and nothing below it; the arrow is bare. The preceding paragraph gives no reagent either, only 'gemäß bekannten Methoden'.

drawings.notes: Schema 2: replacement of the halogen of L-Hal in (IV) by R1 to give (III). Read as the invention's route because the preceding paragraph presents it as the way to obtain the invention's intermediates of formula (III) where R1 is alkoxy; nothing on the page frames it as prior art. No SMILES because R, R1, R2, R4, R5, R6, L and Hal are all undefined on this page. Both benzene rings here are drawn with the substituent set R2, R4, R5, R6, which is NOT the set drawn on the (III) of Schema 1 higher up the same page; see discrepancies.

discrepancies.what: Formula (III) is drawn twice on this page and the two drawings label the benzene ring differently, so the same formula number carries two different substituent sets.
discrepancies.drawing_says: Schema 1, structure (III): going round the ring from the acyl carbon C1 in the direction of R2, the labels are R2 at C2, L-R1 at C3, R3 at C4, R4 at C5, R5 at C6.
discrepancies.text_says: Schema 2, structure (III) (and the (IV) it comes from): the same traversal gives R2 at C2, L-R1 at C3 (L-Hal in (IV)), R4 at C4, R5 at C5, R6 at C6. R3 appears in the first drawing and not the second; R6 appears in the second and not the first. Both readings were taken off the scan at 4x zoom and both are clearly legible, so this is a difference between the two drawings and not a reading error. Recorded, not resolved.

discrepancies.what: R6 appears on the product of Schema 1 but on nothing in its starting materials, and the scheme shows no reagent that could introduce it.
discrepancies.drawing_says: Structure (I) carries R6 bonded directly to the upper-left ring carbon. Structure (II), the ring that becomes it, carries a C=O at that position and no R6 anywhere. The arrow between them is bare.
discrepancies.text_says: The prose on this page says nothing about R6. It discusses only where the starting materials (II) and (III) come from.

discrepancies.what: The prose paragraph on the preparation of (III) names formula (III) as both product and starting material.
discrepancies.drawing_says: Schema 1 draws (III) as a single structure with a single bare R on its acyl group; nothing on the page draws two distinct members of formula (III).
discrepancies.text_says: 'Verbindungen oben genannter Formel (III) können gemäß bekannten Methoden aus Verbindungen der Formel (III), in der R für Hydroxy oder Alkoxy steht, hergestellt werden.' Whether the first (III) is a misprint for another formula number, or whether the sentence intends two members of (III) differing only in R, is not determinable from this page.

illegible: A small ink smudge, roughly 25 x 20 px, immediately to the right of the R6 label of structure (I) in Schema 1, at approximately x 1200-1225, y 375-395 in the 1653x2339 scan. At 8x zoom it resolves into a few disconnected strokes with a faint tail and no readable character. Notably, marks of the same size are recorded at essentially the same coordinates on p04 and p06 of this run, which suggests a fixed artefact on the scanner rather than page content; it is recorded here because it cannot be read and because it sits close enough to the R6 label that a reader could mistake it for a second superscript.

A single isolated speck in the left margin at approximately x 205, y 152, level with the 'WO 00/21924' of the header, and a matching speck at the right edge at approximately x 1600, y 190. Both are single dots with no structure and belong to no printed line.

The Z-to-Y ring bond in structures (II) and (I) of Schema 1 is not drawn as a clearly visible line; the two letter labels sit adjacent with the (R7)w bond crossing between them. Ring closure at Z-Y is taken from the layout, not from a line that can be seen. This is the same drawing convention noted on p06.
